title: Never Enough
coreMove: Set the point where more stops serving the life you are trying to protect.
sourcePressure: Status competition and rising baselines can keep moving the finish line until success turns into self-destruction.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: Reading enough as laziness, low ambition, or anti-growth thinking.

hook: opening with a generic paycheck scene
opening with a moral lesson about discipline
opening Never Enough with a swapped-in personal finance anecdote
counterintuition: reducing Never Enough to common-sense advice
tryThisNow: write down your values for ninety seconds
asking for a generic money reflection instead of the enough move
examples: reusing visible anchors from adjacent chapters instead of enough and status competition

exampleSpecs.domain: a boutique law partner deciding whether to chase a bigger client that will consume every weekend
exampleSpecs.audience: a partner who already earns enough but keeps moving the target
exampleSpecs.stakes: winning the account may cost the family rhythm the money was meant to protect
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she writes the exact Saturdays the new client would take before signing the pitch letter
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a partner desk with a sealed pitch envelope and a youth soccer schedule

exampleSpecs.domain: a restaurateur offered a second location by investors after the first one finally works
exampleSpecs.audience: an owner sorting ambition from status pressure
exampleSpecs.stakes: expansion could turn a loved restaurant into a fragile debt machine
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: he walks the empty dining room after service and names what would have to disappear for the second lease to work
exampleSpecs.firstImage: chairs upside down on tables after the last reservation leaves

exampleSpecs.domain: an auction-house specialist bidding on art for personal status
exampleSpecs.audience: a specialist who knows the market but not her own stop condition
exampleSpecs.stakes: one extra bid could turn knowledge into humiliation
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: she writes her walk-away price on the back of the paddle before the bidding starts and keeps it visible
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a numbered bidding paddle resting on a catalog page

exampleSpecs.domain: a nonprofit executive weighing naming rights against mission control
exampleSpecs.audience: a leader tempted by a gift that changes the institution's priorities
exampleSpecs.stakes: the donation may buy budget relief at the price of independence

exampleSpecs.domain: a professional cyclist deciding whether to use a risky supplement after missing a podium bonus
exampleSpecs.audience: an athlete defining enough before comparison takes over
exampleSpecs.stakes: a career can be lost chasing the gap between good and celebrated

exampleSpecs.firstImage: a race contract beside an unopened silver supplement packet

exampleSpecs.domain: a family-owned marina deciding whether to add luxury slips that price out longtime boaters
